t.why: Taiwanese companies handle most of the world's most advanced chip contract manufacturing, so the supply of smartphones, servers and AI chips depends on Taiwanese fabs. Chips and electronic parts make up a large share of exports, so the economy moves with the global tech cycle and AI investment. It is a member of the World Trade Organization and APEC, and the seas off Taiwan are a main shipping route from Korea and Japan to Southeast Asia and Europe.
t.rel: Its chip and server supply chains tie it closely to American, Japanese, Korean and European companies, and its largest trade flows are with China and the US.
t.korea: Taiwan and Korea compete in chips and displays while buying parts and equipment from each other. In October 2026 Korea exported $8.77bn of goods to Taiwan, its third-largest market after China and the US. Tourism is brisk, and Korean dramas, music and cosmetics are very popular in Taiwan.
t.know: Taipei's National Palace Museum holds hundreds of thousands of artifacts collected by China's imperial dynasties and draws crowds of tourists every year.
etext: Taiwanese companies handle most of the world's most advanced chip contract manufacturing. Chips designed by companies such as Apple and Nvidia are made in Taiwanese fabs. Its chip packaging and design firms are strong too.
Taiwanese companies assemble most of the servers that go into AI data centers. Its supply chains for electronic parts and computer peripherals are dense.
The economy leans heavily on chips and electronic parts, so it swings with the global tech cycle. It is also building plants abroad, including in the US and Japan, near big customers.
